nepal.intro: Nepal is the simplest foreign trip for most Indian families, with no visa, Indian rupees accepted in many places and short flights to Kathmandu. A first visit usually combines darshan at Pashupatinath and the old squares of the Kathmandu Valley with the lakes of Pokhara, while pilgrims often add Muktinath, Janakpur or Lumbini.

destinations.name: Kathmandu Durbar Square
destinations.blurb: The old royal square of the capital, lined with pagoda-roofed temples, palace courtyards and the house of the Kumari.

destinations.name: Bhaktapur Durbar Square
destinations.blurb: A well-kept Newar town east of Kathmandu, known for its five-storey Nyatapola temple, woodcarving and juju dhau curd.

destinations.name: Patan Durbar Square
destinations.blurb: A compact square of stone and brick temples across the river from Kathmandu, with a fine museum in the old palace.

destinations.name: Pokhara
destinations.blurb: A relaxed lakeside town on Phewa Lake, with boating, paragliding and the Annapurna range on the skyline on clear days.

destinations.name: Sarangkot
destinations.blurb: A hilltop above Pokhara where visitors gather before dawn to watch the sun light up Machhapuchhre and the Annapurnas.

destinations.name: Chitwan National Park
destinations.blurb: Lowland forest and grassland in the south, home to one-horned rhinos, with jeep safaris and canoe rides on the Rapti River.

destinations.name: Nagarkot
destinations.blurb: A ridge on the edge of the Kathmandu Valley with wide Himalayan views at sunrise, about an hour and a half from the city.

devotional.name: Pashupatinath Temple
devotional.blurb: Nepal's most sacred Shiva temple on the Bagmati River in Kathmandu, with an evening aarti on the ghats.

devotional.name: Muktinath Temple
devotional.blurb: A Vishnu temple at about 3,700 metres in Mustang, revered by Hindus and Buddhists, with 108 water spouts for a ritual bath.

devotional.name: Janaki Mandir
devotional.blurb: A white marble temple in Janakpur dedicated to Sita, built in the early 1900s at the place traditionally held to be her birthplace.

devotional.name: Lumbini
devotional.blurb: The birthplace of the Buddha, with the Maya Devi Temple, the Ashoka pillar and monasteries built by many Buddhist countries.

devotional.name: Manakamana Temple
devotional.blurb: A hilltop temple to the goddess Bhagwati on the Kathmandu–Pokhara road, reached by a cable car ride over the Trishuli valley.

dishes.name: Dal Bhat
dishes.blurb: The everyday Nepali meal of rice, lentil soup, vegetable curry and pickle, often with free refills.

dishes.name: Momo
dishes.blurb: Steamed dumplings filled with chicken, buffalo or vegetables, served with a spicy tomato and sesame chutney.

dishes.name: Aloo Tama
dishes.blurb: A tangy curry of potatoes, fermented bamboo shoots and black-eyed beans.

dishes.name: Sel Roti
dishes.blurb: A ring-shaped, lightly sweet rice-flour bread fried in oil, made especially during Tihar and Dashain.

dishes.name: Choila
dishes.blurb: A Newar dish of grilled buffalo meat marinated with mustard oil, chilli and spices.

highlights: Evening aarti on the Bagmati at Pashupatinath
Sunrise over the Annapurnas from Sarangkot
Boating on Phewa Lake in Pokhara
Early-morning mountain flight past Everest
Jeep safari to spot rhinos in Chitwan
Cable car ride up to Manakamana Temple
nepal.indianTraveller: Vegetarian and Indian food is easy to find across Nepal, flights from Hyderabad usually connect via Delhi and take around 5 hours in total, Indian plugs fit, and smaller Indian rupee notes are widely accepted alongside Nepalese rupees.

bhutan.currency: Bhutanese ngultrum (BTN), pegged to the Indian rupee
bhutan.intro: Bhutan is a calm, unhurried Himalayan kingdom where monasteries, fortress-dzongs and farmhouses still follow traditional styles. Indian travellers need no visa, and the Indian rupee is accepted at par, which keeps things simple. Most trips follow a loop of Paro, Thimphu and Punakha, with the hike to Tiger's Nest as the highlight.

destinations.name: Thimphu
destinations.blurb: A small, walkable capital with the weekend farmers' market, the Folk Heritage Museum and craft shops selling hand-woven textiles.

destinations.name: Dochula Pass
destinations.blurb: A mountain pass on the Thimphu–Punakha road marked by 108 memorial chortens, with views of the eastern Himalaya on clear days.

destinations.name: Punakha Suspension Bridge
destinations.blurb: One of the longest suspension bridges in Bhutan, strung with prayer flags across the Po Chhu river.

destinations.name: Phobjikha Valley
destinations.blurb: A wide glacial valley in central Bhutan where black-necked cranes arrive from Tibet to spend the winter.

destinations.name: Chele La Pass
destinations.blurb: The highest motorable pass in Bhutan, between Paro and Haa, with prayer flags and views towards Jomolhari.

destinations.name: Motithang Takin Preserve
destinations.blurb: A hillside enclosure above Thimphu where visitors can see the takin, Bhutan's unusual national animal.

devotional.name: Paro Taktsang
devotional.blurb: The Tiger's Nest monastery, clinging to a cliff about 900 metres above the Paro valley, reached by a steep hike of a few hours.

devotional.name: Punakha Dzong
devotional.blurb: A grand 17th-century fortress-monastery where the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu rivers meet, especially pretty in spring with jacaranda in bloom.

devotional.name: Buddha Dordenma
devotional.blurb: A giant gilded statue of the seated Buddha on a hill above Thimphu, holding thousands of smaller Buddha figures inside.

devotional.name: Kyichu Lhakhang
devotional.blurb: One of the oldest temples in Bhutan, near Paro, traditionally dated to the 7th century.

devotional.name: Chimi Lhakhang
devotional.blurb: A small hilltop temple near Punakha, reached by a walk through rice fields, visited by couples praying for children.

dishes.name: Ema Datshi
dishes.blurb: Bhutan's national dish of green or red chillies cooked in a melted local cheese sauce, eaten with rice.

dishes.name: Kewa Datshi
dishes.blurb: A milder cousin of ema datshi made with potatoes and cheese, popular with visitors who find chillies too hot.

dishes.name: Bhutanese Red Rice
dishes.blurb: A nutty, slightly sticky red rice grown in the Paro and Punakha valleys, served with almost every meal.

dishes.name: Phaksha Paa
dishes.blurb: Pork cooked with dried red chillies and radish or greens.

dishes.name: Jasha Maru
dishes.blurb: A spicy chicken stew with tomato, onion, garlic and ginger.

highlights: Hike to the Tiger's Nest monastery
Watching an archery match, the national sport
Crossing Dochula Pass with its 108 chortens
Black-necked cranes in Phobjikha in winter
Dinner at a traditional farmhouse
A masked-dance tshechu festival, if dates allow
bhutan.indianTraveller: Indian and vegetarian meals are standard in most Bhutan hotels, flights to Paro connect via Delhi or Kolkata and take about 5–6 hours from Hyderabad, and Indian rupees are accepted at par, though carrying smaller notes is easier; Indian plugs usually fit.

kazakhstan.intro: Kazakhstan has become a popular short trip for Indian families thanks to visa-free entry and direct flights from Delhi to Almaty. Almaty sits right under the snowy Tien Shan, so mountain lakes, cable cars and canyons are all within a day trip of a modern, green city.

destinations.name: Almaty
destinations.blurb: The largest city, with tree-lined avenues, Panfilov Park, the Green Bazaar and cafes set against snowy peaks.

destinations.name: Kok Tobe
destinations.blurb: A hill above Almaty reached by cable car, with a viewpoint, small rides for children and restaurants.

destinations.name: Medeu and Shymbulak
destinations.blurb: A high-altitude ice rink and, above it, a ski resort reached by gondola, with snow in winter and cool walks in summer.

destinations.name: Big Almaty Lake
destinations.blurb: A turquoise reservoir at about 2,500 metres in the mountains south of Almaty, with peaks rising on all sides.

destinations.name: Charyn Canyon
destinations.blurb: A red rock canyon about three hours from Almaty, where the Valley of Castles trail leads down to the Charyn River.

destinations.name: Kolsai and Kaindy Lakes
destinations.blurb: Mountain lakes near the Kyrgyz border; Kaindy is known for the dead spruce trunks rising out of its water.

destinations.name: Astana
destinations.blurb: The futuristic capital on the steppe, with the Baiterek tower and the Khan Shatyr tent-shaped mall.

devotional.name: Ascension Cathedral, Almaty
devotional.blurb: A colourful wooden Russian Orthodox cathedral in Panfilov Park, completed in 1907 and still standing after a major earthquake.

devotional.name: Central Mosque of Almaty
devotional.blurb: A large white mosque with blue domes near the Green Bazaar, open to respectful visitors outside prayer times.

devotional.name: Hazret Sultan Mosque
devotional.blurb: One of the largest mosques in Central Asia, in Astana, built in white marble with gold-trimmed domes.

devotional.name: Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi
devotional.blurb: A huge 14th-century tiled mausoleum in Turkistan, built under Timur and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

dishes.name: Beshbarmak
dishes.blurb: The national dish of boiled meat, usually horse or lamb, served over flat noodles with onion broth.

dishes.name: Plov
dishes.blurb: Rice cooked with carrots, onions and lamb or beef in a large cast-iron kazan.

dishes.name: Shelpek
dishes.blurb: Thin, soft flatbreads fried in oil, often served with tea.

dishes.name: Kurt
dishes.blurb: Small, hard balls of dried salted cheese, a common snack for road trips.

dishes.name: Kumys
dishes.blurb: Lightly fermented mare's milk, a traditional drink of the steppe that is sour and slightly fizzy.

highlights: Cable car up Kok Tobe at sunset
Day trip to Charyn Canyon
Gondola ride to Shymbulak
Photos at Big Almaty Lake
Dried fruit and nut shopping at the Green Bazaar
Ice skating at Medeu in winter
kazakhstan.indianTraveller: Almaty and Astana have several Indian restaurants, though local food is meat-heavy so vegetarians should ask clearly, flights from Hyderabad connect via Delhi and take around 6–7 hours, plugs are the European two-pin type, and US dollars are easy to exchange for tenge.

uzbekistan.intro: Uzbekistan holds some of the finest Silk Road cities, and Indian travellers often feel a connection here, since Timur, buried in Samarkand, was an ancestor of Babur and the Mughals. Fast trains link Tashkent, Samarkand and Bukhara, which makes a week-long tour comfortable for families and senior travellers.

destinations.name: Registan
destinations.blurb: The great square of Samarkand, framed by three tiled madrasas from the 15th to 17th centuries and lit up in the evenings.

destinations.name: Gur-e-Amir
destinations.blurb: The ribbed blue-domed mausoleum of Timur in Samarkand, whose design influenced Mughal tombs such as the Taj Mahal.

destinations.name: Ulugh Beg Observatory
destinations.blurb: Remains of the 15th-century observatory of the astronomer-king Ulugh Beg, with a large curved sextant cut into the hill.

destinations.name: Ark of Bukhara
destinations.blurb: A massive mud-brick fortress that was home to the rulers of Bukhara for centuries, now housing small museums.

destinations.name: Itchan Kala
destinations.blurb: The walled inner town of Khiva, packed with minarets, madrasas and palaces, best seen from the walls at sunset.

destinations.name: Chorsu Bazaar
destinations.blurb: A domed market in old Tashkent selling spices, dried fruit, nuts, bread and fresh produce.

devotional.name: Shah-i-Zinda
devotional.blurb: An avenue of richly tiled mausoleums in Samarkand, linked to Qusam ibn Abbas, a cousin of the Prophet Muhammad.

devotional.name: Bibi-Khanym Mosque
devotional.blurb: A vast 15th-century mosque in Samarkand built by Timur after his campaigns in India, partly restored in recent decades.

devotional.name: Po-i-Kalyan
devotional.blurb: The central ensemble of Bukhara, with the 12th-century Kalyan Minaret, the Kalyan Mosque and the Mir-i-Arab Madrasa.

devotional.name: Hazrati Imam Complex
devotional.blurb: A religious complex in Tashkent whose library holds an early Quran manuscript traditionally linked to Caliph Uthman.

dishes.name: Plov
dishes.blurb: The national dish of rice cooked with carrots, onions, chickpeas and lamb, made in huge pots for weddings and gatherings.

dishes.name: Samsa
dishes.blurb: Flaky pastries baked in a tandoor, usually filled with minced lamb and onion.

dishes.name: Lagman
dishes.blurb: Hand-pulled noodles in a rich broth with beef or lamb and vegetables.

dishes.name: Non
dishes.blurb: Round, stamped Uzbek bread baked against the walls of a clay tandoor, sold fresh in every bazaar.

dishes.name: Achichuk
dishes.blurb: A simple salad of sliced tomatoes, onions and herbs, served alongside plov.

highlights: The Registan lit up in the evening
High-speed Afrosiyob train to Samarkand
Visiting Timur's tomb at Gur-e-Amir
Walking the walls of Khiva at sunset
Silk and suzani shopping in Bukhara
The ornate stations of the Tashkent Metro
uzbekistan.indianTraveller: Tashkent has a good number of Indian restaurants and Samarkand and Bukhara have a few, though vegetarians should carry some snacks for days on the road, flights from Hyderabad connect via Delhi and take about 6 hours, plugs are the European two-pin type, and clean US dollar notes are the easiest currency to exchange.

kyrgyzstan.intro: Kyrgyzstan is a mountain country of high pastures, lakes and nomadic traditions, best for families who enjoy the outdoors. Summer is the season for yurt stays, horse rides and swims in Issyk-Kul, while Bishkek is a relaxed base with parks and bazaars.

destinations.name: Ala-Archa Nature Park
destinations.blurb: A mountain valley less than an hour from Bishkek with walking trails beside a glacier-fed river and juniper forest.

destinations.name: Issyk-Kul
destinations.blurb: A huge alpine lake that never freezes, with beaches and resorts around Cholpon-Ata on its northern shore.

destinations.name: Cholpon-Ata Petroglyphs
destinations.blurb: An open-air field of boulders carved with ibex, deer and hunters, some thousands of years old.

destinations.name: Burana Tower
destinations.blurb: An 11th-century minaret near Tokmok, all that remains of the old city of Balasagun, with a field of carved stone figures nearby.

destinations.name: Jeti-Oguz Gorge
destinations.blurb: A valley near Karakol known for the red sandstone cliffs called the Seven Bulls and the Broken Heart rock.

destinations.name: Song-Kul
destinations.blurb: A high mountain lake at about 3,000 metres where herders graze horses in summer and visitors stay in yurt camps.

destinations.name: Skazka Canyon
destinations.blurb: The Fairy Tale Canyon on the south shore of Issyk-Kul, with wind-carved red and orange rock formations.

devotional.name: Holy Trinity Cathedral, Karakol
devotional.blurb: A wooden Russian Orthodox cathedral from the late 19th century, still used for services.

devotional.name: Dungan Mosque
devotional.blurb: A Chinese-style wooden mosque in Karakol built by the Dungan community in the early 1900s, famously without metal nails.

devotional.name: Sulaiman-Too
devotional.blurb: A rocky sacred mountain in the city of Osh, a pilgrimage site for centuries and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

dishes.name: Beshbarmak
dishes.blurb: Boiled lamb or horse meat chopped and served over flat noodles with onions and broth.

dishes.name: Ashlan-Fu
dishes.blurb: A cold, spicy noodle soup from Karakol with starch jelly, vinegar and egg.

dishes.name: Lagman
dishes.blurb: Hand-pulled noodles stir-fried or served in broth with meat and vegetables.

dishes.name: Tandyr Nan
dishes.blurb: Round bread baked in a clay tandyr oven, eaten at every meal.

dishes.name: Kymyz
dishes.blurb: Fermented mare's milk, sold at roadside yurts in summer.

highlights: A night in a yurt camp at Song-Kul
Horse riding on high summer pastures
An eagle-hunting demonstration
A swim in Issyk-Kul
Climbing the stairs inside Burana Tower
Exploring Osh Bazaar in Bishkek
kyrgyzstan.indianTraveller: Local food is mostly meat, but Bishkek has some Indian restaurants thanks to its many Indian students, flights from Hyderabad connect via Delhi, Almaty or Tashkent and take about 7–9 hours, plugs are the European two-pin type, and US dollars are easy to change for som.

azerbaijan.intro: Azerbaijan pairs the walled old town and modern skyline of Baku with green mountain towns in the Caucasus. Indian visitors often seek out the Ateshgah, a fire temple near Baku built and used by Hindu and Zoroastrian traders from India, which still carries inscriptions in Sanskrit and Punjabi. Baku is a short trip with an easy e-Visa.

destinations.name: Icherisheher
destinations.blurb: Baku's walled Old City, with the Maiden Tower, the Palace of the Shirvanshahs, caravanserais and carpet shops.

destinations.name: Baku Boulevard
destinations.blurb: A long seaside promenade on the Caspian with parks, cafes and evening views of the Flame Towers lighting up.

destinations.name: Heydar Aliyev Center
destinations.blurb: A museum and cultural centre designed by Zaha Hadid, known for its sweeping white curves.

destinations.name: Gobustan National Park
destinations.blurb: A rocky reserve south of Baku with thousands of ancient rock carvings, often combined with a visit to nearby mud volcanoes.

destinations.name: Yanar Dag
destinations.blurb: A hillside on the Absheron Peninsula where natural gas has burned continuously for decades, best seen after dark.

destinations.name: Gabala
destinations.blurb: A green mountain town with the Tufandag cable car, lakes and walks in the forest.

destinations.name: Sheki
destinations.blurb: An old Silk Road town known for the painted Palace of the Sheki Khans and its stained-glass shebeke windows.

devotional.name: Ateshgah of Baku
devotional.blurb: A fire temple in Surakhani built by Indian traders in the 17th and 18th centuries, with prayer cells and Sanskrit and Punjabi inscriptions.

devotional.name: Bibi-Heybat Mosque
devotional.blurb: A large mosque on the Caspian shore south of Baku, rebuilt in the 1990s on the site of a 13th-century shrine.

devotional.name: Taza Pir Mosque
devotional.blurb: The main Friday mosque of Baku, built in the early 20th century with a richly decorated interior.

devotional.name: Church of Kish
devotional.blurb: A small, restored stone church in a village near Sheki, linked to the early Christian history of Caucasian Albania.

dishes.name: Shah Plov
dishes.blurb: Saffron rice with lamb, chestnuts and dried fruit baked inside a crisp lavash crust.

dishes.name: Dolma
dishes.blurb: Vine leaves or vegetables stuffed with minced lamb, rice and herbs.

dishes.name: Qutab
dishes.blurb: Thin folded flatbreads cooked on a griddle, with a vegetarian version filled with fresh greens and herbs.

dishes.name: Dushbara
dishes.blurb: Tiny lamb dumplings served in a clear broth flavoured with dried mint.

dishes.name: Tea with Jam
dishes.blurb: Black tea served in pear-shaped glasses with small dishes of cherry, quince or walnut jam.

highlights: Funicular ride up to the Flame Towers viewpoint
An evening walk on Baku Boulevard
Seeing the burning hillside at Yanar Dag
Visiting the Ateshgah fire temple
Tufandag cable car in Gabala
The mud volcanoes near Gobustan
azerbaijan.indianTraveller: Baku has many Indian restaurants with full vegetarian menus, flights from Hyderabad usually connect via Delhi or a Gulf hub and take about 7 hours, plugs are the European two-pin type, and manat is easy to get from ATMs or by exchanging US dollars.

georgia.intro: Georgia offers mountain drives, old churches and a lively capital in a compact country that is easy to tour by road. Indian families usually combine Tbilisi with a day or two in Kazbegi and Gudauri, and many add Batumi on the Black Sea. Georgian food has plenty of bean, cheese and vegetable dishes, which helps vegetarians.

destinations.name: Old Tbilisi
destinations.blurb: Narrow lanes of carved wooden balconies, the domed sulphur baths of Abanotubani and a cable car up to Narikala Fortress.

destinations.name: Ananuri Fortress
destinations.blurb: A 17th-century fortress with two churches beside the turquoise Zhinvali reservoir on the Georgian Military Road.

destinations.name: Gudauri
destinations.blurb: A ski resort high on the Georgian Military Road, used for skiing in winter and paragliding and walks in summer.

destinations.name: Stepantsminda
destinations.blurb: A mountain town also known as Kazbegi, at the foot of Mount Kazbek near the Russian border.

destinations.name: Sighnaghi
destinations.blurb: A small hilltop town in the wine region of Kakheti with old walls and views over the Alazani Valley.

destinations.name: Uplistsikhe
destinations.blurb: An ancient cave town cut into the rock above the Mtkvari River near Gori.

destinations.name: Batumi
destinations.blurb: A Black Sea resort city with a long seaside boulevard, botanical garden and modern architecture.

devotional.name: Gergeti Trinity Church
devotional.blurb: A 14th-century church on a ridge above Stepantsminda with Mount Kazbek behind it, reached by a short drive or hike.

devotional.name: Jvari Monastery
devotional.blurb: A 6th-century church on a hilltop above Mtskheta, overlooking the meeting of the Aragvi and Mtkvari rivers.

devotional.name: Svetitskhoveli Cathedral
devotional.blurb: The great 11th-century cathedral of Mtskheta, the old capital, and one of the holiest sites in Georgia.

devotional.name: Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi
devotional.blurb: The large modern cathedral known as Sameba, completed in 2004, with gold domes visible across the city.

devotional.name: Bodbe Monastery
devotional.blurb: A convent among cypress trees just outside Sighnaghi, where Saint Nino, who brought Christianity to Georgia, is buried.

dishes.name: Imeruli Khachapuri
dishes.blurb: A round bread filled with melted Georgian cheese, sold in every bakery and restaurant.

dishes.name: Khinkali
dishes.blurb: Large twisted dumplings filled with spiced meat and broth, eaten by hand.

dishes.name: Lobio
dishes.blurb: Red beans stewed with herbs, garlic and spices, traditionally served in a clay pot.

dishes.name: Badrijani Nigvzit
dishes.blurb: Fried aubergine slices rolled around a walnut and garlic paste, topped with pomegranate seeds.

dishes.name: Mtsvadi
dishes.blurb: Georgian skewers of pork or lamb grilled over vine cuttings.

highlights: Cable car up to Narikala Fortress
Drive along the Georgian Military Road
Snow or paragliding at Gudauri
A visit to the sulphur baths in Tbilisi
Wine and churchkhela tasting in Kakheti
Evening walk on the Batumi seafront
georgia.indianTraveller: Tbilisi and Batumi have several Indian restaurants and local menus include many vegetarian dishes, flights from Hyderabad connect via Dubai or Delhi and take about 7–9 hours, plugs are the European two-pin type, and lari is easy to get from ATMs or by exchanging US dollars.

armenia.intro: Armenia is one of the oldest Christian countries, and its stone monasteries in mountain settings are the main reason to visit. Yerevan is a friendly, walkable base, and most sights, including Garni, Geghard, Khor Virap and Lake Sevan, are easy day trips. The e-Visa or visa on arrival makes planning straightforward for Indian travellers.

destinations.name: Cascade Complex
destinations.blurb: A giant white stairway in Yerevan lined with sculptures and fountains, with city views and Mount Ararat on clear days from the top.

destinations.name: Republic Square
destinations.blurb: The grand central square of Yerevan, built in pink tuff stone, with musical fountains on summer evenings.

destinations.name: Matenadaran
destinations.blurb: A museum and research institute holding thousands of ancient Armenian manuscripts, many beautifully illuminated.

destinations.name: Garni Temple
destinations.blurb: A 1st-century Greco-Roman style temple on a cliff above a gorge, the only standing building of its kind in the former Soviet Union.

destinations.name: Lake Sevan
destinations.blurb: A large blue lake at about 1,900 metres, popular for summer swims, boat rides and fresh fish lunches.

destinations.name: Dilijan
destinations.blurb: A forested hill town with restored old streets, sometimes called the Switzerland of Armenia.

destinations.name: Wings of Tatev
destinations.blurb: One of the longest reversible cable cars in the world, gliding over the Vorotan gorge to Tatev Monastery.

devotional.name: Khor Virap
devotional.blurb: A monastery near the Turkish border with an outstanding view of Mount Ararat, built where Saint Gregory was imprisoned in a pit.

devotional.name: Geghard Monastery
devotional.blurb: A UNESCO-listed monastery partly carved out of the rock in a mountain gorge near Garni.

devotional.name: Etchmiadzin Cathedral
devotional.blurb: The mother cathedral of the Armenian Apostolic Church, traditionally dated to the early 4th century.

devotional.name: Sevanavank
devotional.blurb: Two small stone churches on a peninsula on Lake Sevan, with views across the water.

devotional.name: Tatev Monastery
devotional.blurb: A 9th-century monastery on the edge of a deep gorge in southern Armenia, once an important centre of learning.

dishes.name: Khorovats
dishes.blurb: Armenian barbecue of pork, lamb or chicken grilled on skewers over charcoal.

dishes.name: Dolma
dishes.blurb: Grape leaves or cabbage stuffed with minced meat and rice, served with garlic yoghurt.

dishes.name: Lavash
dishes.blurb: Thin soft flatbread baked in a clay tonir oven, listed by UNESCO as part of Armenian heritage.

dishes.name: Ghapama
dishes.blurb: A whole pumpkin stuffed with rice, dried fruit, nuts and honey, baked until soft.

dishes.name: Harissa
dishes.blurb: A thick, slow-cooked porridge of wheat and chicken, traditionally made for festivals.

highlights: The Wings of Tatev cable car ride
Mount Ararat views from Khor Virap
Watching lavash being baked in a tonir
Climbing the Cascade in Yerevan
Musical fountains at Republic Square
Weekend crafts at the Vernissage market
armenia.indianTraveller: Yerevan has a growing number of Indian restaurants and local meals include vegetarian salads, breads and stews, flights from Hyderabad connect via Dubai or Delhi and take about 7–9 hours, plugs are the European two-pin type, and dram is easy to get from ATMs or by exchanging US dollars.
